originalTitle: The blue-collar AI job market is booming. Will data center backlash make it go bust?
summary: The public has soured on AI data centers and states are slowing development, but for HVAC, plumbing, welding, and electrical workers, it's been a jobs boom.
content:
When most people think of AI and jobs, the conversation often pivots to which occupations are most likely to be obliterated by its arrival. But, at least for some professions, the AI boom has been an employment one too.

AI is creating jobs in a variety of trades that prop up the sprawling ecosystem that powers giants like Anthropic , Meta, Amazon, OpenAI, and others.

The construction and maintaining of data centers and the entire AI ecosystem is requiring a new generation of HVAC technicians, construction workers, line workers, and pipefitters.

"These are occupations that are becoming increasingly important to the AI economy," said Maria Flynn, president and CEO of national nonprofit Jobs for the Future. While data centers are the part that gets the publicity, they are only one piece of a much larger puzzle, requiring upgrades in transportation and modernization of the energy grid. "We are seeing major sources of demand that are converging at the same time," Flynn said.

The skilled jobs often come with attractive pay. Flynn said an apprentice level technician can take home $40,000 to $60,000, with experienced electricians commanding north of $100,000.

Nicole Bachaud, labor economist at online employment marketplace ZipRecruiter, is seeing salaries even higher for more specialized, high skill roles. Bachaud said that the mean minimum salary for data center jobs spiked by 125.1% year-over-year to nearly $208,000.

"This is suggesting that highly specialized, top-tier engineering roles are pulling the overall average up drastically," Bachaud said.

While many traditional blue-collar workers are seeing a boost, including truckers , the biggest blue collar beneficiaries, according to Bachaud's data, are welders and pipefitters. Postings for those jobs are up 164% year over year. While that could be partly the result of a small sample size as more data centers are built, even if each one only needs a few pipefitters, the demand for these roles will increase, she said. The construction demand is also uneven with some places getting in on it more than others. Houston and Birmingham have seen particularly robust growth.

"Places with more land to expand and build, which are often places where building regulations make development easier, cheaper, and faster, will likely be where expansion continues, versus coastal hubs that have higher costs and more regulatory burdens," Bachaud said.

That means an electrician or pipefitter in Birmingham will probably have more of a buyer's market than one in Boston.

None of this surprises Justin Sinkovich, associate professor and associate director of the School of Business and Entrepreneurship at Columbia College Chicago. In his view, the usual AI jobs narrative of displacement is incomplete, with the data center counter-story as one example.

While AI may automate some work , its deployment depends on the buildout of infrastructure, including not only data centers but also substations, cooling systems, water, and piping infrastructure, which AI cannot build.

"Positive effects on the labor market are already visible, with an increased demand for cooling and HVAC engineers, industrial automation technicians, and traditional trade workers like construction workers and electricians. HVAC-engineering wages have risen, and many technical professionals entering data-center roles are seeing a pay premium," Sinkovich said.

He pointed to Louisiana as a specific example, where both Amazon and Meta have massive projects.

"Amazon committed $12 billion to a new data center with 540 new on-site jobs, including 1,700 electricians, technicians, and security personnel. Meta's Hyperion project in Louisiana is $27 billion," Sinkovich said. "These projects create demand for on-site workers and therefore cannot be offshored or conducted remotely, unlike manufacturing and software," he added.

He also said there is a longer-term story of AI enabling more decentralized and dynamic energy systems. This not only improves energy efficiency but also creates additional work to build smart controls, battery systems, microgrids, and distributed energy infrastructure.

Economic optimism vs. public skepticism

Recent research from global real estate services firm Cushman & Wakefield indicates that every 100MW of new data center development creates nearly 1,300 jobs in the local economy, generating approximately $110 million in annual wages, $344 million in gross output, and $187 million in gross regional product. And many of these jobs aren't ones requiring a diploma. In fact, many of them are better suited to a path through trade school.

But the optimistic shovels on the ground analysis don't match the national mood. Seventy percent of Americans oppose a data center being built in their local area, according to Gallup, and a New York Times/Siena poll conducted this month found roughly two-thirds opposed regardless of party — Democrats, independents and Republicans alike.

Even where data centers are proceeding at a robust clip and creating the most jobs public opinion has turned against them. Fifty-seven percent of voters oppose one in their own community, according to a Texas Politics Project poll , enough that some experts see Democrats gaining ground in the Lone Star State. According to Data Center Watch , at least 75 data center projects worth roughly $130 billion have already been blocked or delayed this year as the backlash spreads.

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, currently up for reelection, recently issued a data center grid approval moratorium and halt on new environmental permits. New York Governor Kathy Hochul recently implemented the first statewide ban on new data centers.

chineseTitle: 蓝领 AI 就业市场正在蓬勃发展。数据中心的强烈反对会导致其破产吗？
chineseSummary: 公众对人工智能数据中心的态度已经变差，各州正在放慢发展速度，但对于暖通空调、管道、焊接和电气工人来说，这是就业热潮。
chineseContent:
当大多数人想到人工智能和工作时，话题往往会转向哪些职业最有可能因人工智能的到来而消失。但是，至少对于某些职业来说，人工智能的繁荣也带来了就业机会。

人工智能正在各个行业创造就业机会，支撑着庞大的生态系统，为 Anthropic、Meta、亚马逊、OpenAI 等巨头提供动力。

数据中心和整个人工智能生态系统的建设和维护需要新一代的暖通空调技术人员、建筑工人、生产线工人和管道安装工。

“这些职业对于人工智能经济来说变得越来越重要，”全国性非营利组织“未来就业”总裁兼首席执行官玛丽亚·弗林 (Maria Flynn) 表示。虽然数据中心是广为人知的部分，但它们只是更大难题的一小部分，需要交通升级和能源网格现代化。 “我们看到主要的需求来源正在同时汇聚，”弗林说。

技术性工作通常具有有吸引力的薪酬。 Flynn 表示，学徒级技术人员的年薪可达 4 万至 6 万美元，而经验丰富的电工年薪则可达 10 万美元以上。

在线就业市场 ZipRecruiter 的劳动经济学家 Nicole Bachaud 认为，更专业、高技能的职位的薪水甚至更高。 Bachaud 表示，数据中心工作的平均最低工资同比飙升 125.1%，达到近 208,000 美元。

巴乔德说：“这表明高度专业化的顶级工程职位正在大幅提高总体平均水平。”

虽然包括卡车司机在内的许多传统蓝领工人的收入有所增加，但根据巴绍的数据，最大的蓝领受益者是焊工和管道安装工。这些职位的招聘数量同比增长 164%。她说，虽然这可能部分是由于随着更多数据中心的建立，样本量较小，但即使每个数据中心只需要几个管道安装工，对这些角色的需求也会增加。建设需求也参差不齐，有的地方投入较多。休斯顿和伯明翰的增长尤其强劲。

巴肖德说：“那些有更多土地可供扩建和建设的地方，通常是建筑法规使开发变得更容易、更便宜和更快的地方，很可能会继续扩张，而沿海中心的成本更高，监管负担更重。”

这意味着伯明翰的电工或管道安装工可能比波士顿的电工或管道安装工更容易进入买方市场。

芝加哥哥伦比亚学院商业与创业学院副教授兼副主任贾斯汀·辛科维奇（Justin Sinkovich）对此并不感到惊讶。在他看来，通常的人工智能工作岗位转移叙述是不完整的，数据中心的反面故事就是一个例子。

虽然人工智能可以使一些工作自动化，但其部署取决于基础设施的建设，不仅包括数据中心，还包括人工智能无法建设的变电站、冷却系统、水和管道基础设施。

“对劳动力市场的积极影响已经显而易见，对冷却和暖通空调工程师、工业自动化技术人员以及建筑工人和电工等传统贸易工人的需求增加。暖通空调工程工资上涨，许多进入数据中心职位的技术专业人员都看到了工资溢价，”辛科维奇说。

他以路易斯安那州为例，亚马逊和 Meta 都在那里开展了大量项目。

“亚马逊承诺投资 120 亿美元建设新数据中心，并提供 540 个新的现场工作岗位，其中包括 1,700 名电工、技术人员和保安人员。Meta 在路易斯安那州的 Hyperion 项目耗资 270 亿美元，”Sinkovich 说。他补充说：“这些项目创造了对现场工人的需求，因此不能像制造和软件那样外包或远程进行。”

他还表示，人工智能可以实现更加分散和动态的能源系统，这是一个长期的故事。这不仅提高了能源效率，还增加了构建智能控制、电池系统、微电网和分布式能源基础设施的额外工作。

经济乐观与公众怀疑

全球房地产服务公司高纬环球 (Cushman & Wakefield) 最近的研究表明，每开发 100 兆瓦的新数据中心将为当地经济创造近 1,300 个就业岗位，产生约 1.1 亿美元的年工资、3.44 亿美元的总产出和 1.87 亿美元的地区生产总值。其中许多工作不需要文凭。事实上，他们中的许多人更适合通过贸易学校学习。

但实地分析的乐观情绪与国民情绪并不相符。据盖洛普称，70% 的美国人反对在当地建立数据中心，而《纽约时报》/锡耶纳本月进行的一项民意调查发现，无论党派如何——民主党、独立人士和共和党，大约三分之二的人都反对。

即使数据中心进展强劲并创造了最多的就业机会，公众舆论也对它们持反对态度。根据德克萨斯州政治项目的一项民意调查，百分之五十七的选民反对自己社区的选民，这足以让一些专家认为民主党在孤星州取得了进展。据 Data Center Watch 称，随着抵制情绪的蔓延，今年至少有 75 个价值约 1,300 亿美元的数据中心项目已被阻止或推迟。

目前正在竞选连任的德克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特 (Greg Abbott) 最近发布了一项数据中心电网暂停审批计划，并停止发放新的环境许可证。纽约州州长 Kathy Hochul 最近实施了第一个全州范围内的新数据中心禁令。

这种情况的动态促使甲骨文本周就其新墨西哥州数据中心项目（更广泛的 Stargate AI 扩建项目的一部分）提交了一份“不可抗力”（即项目可能因特殊情况而推迟的规定）通知，寻求在该设施无法运营的情况下推迟付款。
